scope_boundary: Only sources and action surfaces observed in this operator run are listed as observed. Other services remain conditional until an exact connector action, resource, and permission are confirmed. This catalog guides discovery and normalization; it does not grant access.

sources.revision_strategy: Default branch SHA and repository updated_at; recheck in each scoped cycle.
refresh_steps: Read repository metadata from the exact endpoint.
Record date and source URL.
Compare the current default branch SHA with the last accepted observation.
limitations: A repository read does not imply access to other repositories or private resources.
Read access does not authorize writes.

sources.revision_strategy: Commit SHA, tree SHA, and exact blob SHA per path.
refresh_steps: Resolve current main head.
Fetch the recursive tree for that exact head.
Compare each path/blob identity with the accepted inventory.
limitations: The tree is a snapshot and changes with commits.
Descriptions of file purpose require source review.

sources.revision_strategy: Commit SHA, parent SHA, subject, and author timestamp.
refresh_steps: Fetch a bounded recent commit page.
Record the returned count and page size.
Label topic classification as inferred.
limitations: A page limit does not establish complete history.
Subject-derived categories remain inferred.

sources.revision_strategy: Repository plus issue/PR number and updated_at.
refresh_steps: Fetch the endpoint for the explicitly scoped repository.
Normalize returned items into source envelopes.
Do not equate an empty response with no tasks outside GitHub.
limitations: The observed response was empty.
Other task sources need their own explicit catalog entries.

sources.revision_strategy: Workflow run ID, head SHA, job conclusion.
refresh_steps: Fetch recent runs.
Select the run for the exact target commit.
Read job conclusions/logs before accepting a verification claim.
limitations: A success verifies only the named commit and test scope.
CI success does not establish production readiness.

sources.revision_strategy: Observed date and exact tool-name list per namespace.
refresh_steps: Read the surfaced tool registry at the beginning of a relevant operator run.
Compare namespace and action names to the snapshot.
Resolve the current exact action schema and verify resource access for each actual task.
limitations: Tool definitions are not credentials or permissions.
The surface can change between conversations.
A catalog entry never authorizes workspace scanning or external writes.

sources.revision_strategy: Input ID, requirement revision, and Git commit.
refresh_steps: Capture explicit scope changes as minimal normalized input records.
Separate user statements from assistant inference.
Link changes to affected contexts and work items.
limitations: The full conversation transcript is not canonical data.
Implicit preferences must not become binding rules without review.

sources.locator: Resolve provider, resource and exact action from the current tool registry when a task needs that source.
sources.revision_strategy: Provider-specific source revision or immutable ID returned by the exact read action.
data_types: Task-relevant records defined per integration task.
refresh_steps: Discover the exact current tool action/schema.
Confirm access to the requested resource.
Read only the task-relevant records and preserve source locator/revision.
Add a provider-specific catalog entry if the integration becomes recurring.
limitations: Universal access is not claimed.
Resource IDs and action arguments must not be guessed.
Writes and privileged effects have separate authorization requirements.

sources.revision_strategy: Snapshot ID plus base commit, frozen registry blob SHA, per-source revision and capture timestamp.
refresh_steps: Read exact endpoints with authorized GitHub tools.
Record timestamp, URLs, revisions and base commit.
Normalize against the matching frozen registry fixture.
Compare generated input records with stored records and replay to verify duplicate no-ops.
Commit accepted input records and the cycle report with registry links.
limitations: Snapshot was captured at 2026-10-16T20:12:59Z against base commit de6df318372ed9a009053a23d747f229c4ec2d53.
The empty issue result applies only to state=all&per_page=30.
The successful workflow is evidence for review, not automatic context acceptance or external authorization.

sources.revision_strategy: Verification ID, timestamp, exact resource identity, tool/action names, evidence references and commit/run IDs; refresh after session, permission, or provider changes.
data_types: Task scope and authorization basis per write
Replayable read-only, blocked, and approval-gated examples
refresh_steps: Resolve current exact action schemas from the surfaced tool registry.
Check read and write permissions separately against a specific resource.
Record exact targets, scope, authorization basis, and evidence for each successful action.
Keep unrequested resources in a not_checked or limited disposition.
Run the replayable policy examples and refresh the record when tool or permission state changes.
limitations: Access is proven only for the named resources and successful actions.
Visible tool definitions are not resource permissions.
The record does not grant any permission or authorize a new action.
Repository settings, secrets, deployments, private repositories, and other connected-service resources remain unverified unless separately checked.

refresh_policy: Refresh observations when the source revision changes or when evidence is material to a new decision.
Prefer append-only dated observations rather than overwriting historical claims; mark affected derived context stale.
Every accepted input should retain source locator, revision when available, access boundary, trust status, disposition, and linked contexts/tasks.
The registry and catalog describe capability boundaries; they never grant resource permission.
No backend, persistent queue, API service, or deployment is required during the current phase.
Pure GitHub normalizers and the snapshot runner are implemented at src/scs/adapters/github.py and src/scs/runner.py. They consume caller-supplied API objects and do not fetch the network.
Cycle 0006 captures a fresh scoped GitHub snapshot; four normalized input records under swarm/inputs/IN-GH-*.json are checked against the pure runner output and replayed for duplicate no-ops.

SCS-MATURE-008 records exact resource-specific tool actions and separates read access, scoped writes, and privileged effects. Use swarm/sources/capability-verification-2026-10-26.json as dated evidence, not as a permission grant.
